_meta.description: Rolling stock for Line 5. The trains are ordered: Titagarh Rail Systems holds package CA-241 (trains, signalling, telecom, platform screen doors, depot machinery) for Phases 1 and 2. 'specs' are MMRDA's published figures, shown as rows. Phase 3 and the Line 5A spur are not in this contract.

procurement.value: MMRDA's letter of acceptance, announced by Titagarh to the stock exchanges on 31 Oct 2025
procurement.scope: Design, manufacture, supply and commissioning of the trains, with CBTC signalling and train control, telecom, platform screen doors and depot machinery at Kasheli
procurement.built_at: its plant at Uttarpara, near Kolkata

maintenance.value: Five years of comprehensive maintenance in the award reports; the tender set 15 years after a 2-year defect liability period

procurement.schedule: Execution starts 62 weeks after the contract is signed, and is to be complete within the following 154 weeks (Titagarh's project page): 216 weeks, against the 217 reported.
procurement.notes: Titagarh's own project page lists the order: 132 metro coaches for Line 5, about Rs 2,481 crore. Titagarh was declared the lowest bidder in June 2025 (The Metro Rail Guy, against MMRDA's estimate of Rs 2,640.72 crore from the February 2024 bid invitation). The award reports name Phase 2 as running to Kalyan APMC, the 2017 plan's end.

specs.notes: MMRDA's Line 5 page lists width, height and length under rolling stock; it does not say whether the length is one car or a whole train, so the page shows it as given. Trains and cars per train come from the contract.

traction.value: Traction and train control (TCMS) for the 22 trains, on 25 kV AC overhead power; automation at grade GoA2, upgradable to GoA4
traction.notes: ABB's order from Titagarh (January 2026) covers 40 six-car trains: 22 for Line 5 and 18 for Line 6.

image.caption: The Line 5 train design.
image.notes: Titagarh's project page shows a Mumbai metro picture, all rights reserved, and does not say it is the Line 5 train, so the site links to it and does not copy it. Until a picture with usable terms is found, the page shows a generic drawing.
